title: Why Fuels Burn With a Flame
description: Some fuels dance with flames; others just glow. Discover why to earn ember 8.

content.value: Not Everything Burns With a Flame
Have you noticed that a candle or gas burns with a FLAME, but coal or charcoal often just GLOWS red without much flame? The difference is whether the fuel produces gases (vapours) when heated.

A FLAME is produced only when GASEOUS substances burn. Fuels that turn into vapour (gas) on heating — like wax, kerosene and LPG — burn with a flame. The heat first turns the fuel into vapour, and it is this vapour that burns as a flame.

BURNS WITH A FLAME (makes vapour)   GLOWS, LITTLE FLAME (no vapour)
🕯️  candle wax (melts → vapour)      🪨  coal
⛽  kerosene, LPG                    🪵  charcoal
→ the vapour burns as a flame        → the solid glows red-hot

When a candle burns, the heat melts the wax, then turns it into vapour. This wax vapour rises and burns, producing the familiar flame. Blow out a candle and you can briefly see a trail of white smoke — that's unburnt wax vapour!
Quick rule: substances that vaporise (turn to gas) when heated burn with a flame; those that don't just glow. That's why gas and candles flame, but charcoal glows.

Key Takeaway: A flame is produced only when gaseous (vaporised) substances burn. Fuels that turn into vapour on heating (wax, kerosene, LPG) burn with a flame; solids like coal that don't vaporise just glow.

quiz.question: A flame is produced only when the burning substance is…
quiz.explain: Only gaseous substances burn with a flame. Fuels that vaporise on heating produce flames.

quiz.question: Why does a candle burn with a flame?
options: The wax vaporises and the vapour burns
quiz.explain: Heat turns the wax into vapour, and it is this wax vapour that burns as a flame.

quiz.question: Coal and charcoal often just glow instead of flaming because they…
options: do not produce vapour when heated
quiz.explain: Without vapour there is no flame, so these solids glow red-hot instead.
